name: Ransomware
description: Mass encryption on an endpoint: what raises it, what groups it, what to establish, what to do, and how to prove the pack works here.

correlations.name: One incident per host per encryption burst
correlations.why: Three rules fire on the same burst. Without this an operator gets three alerts for one event, which is worse than the one they had before adopting the pack.

correlations.name: Fold in the shadow-copy deletion that usually precedes it
correlations.why: Deletion often lands minutes ahead of encryption. Grouped, the timeline reads as one attack; separate, the earlier alert looks like unrelated admin work.

investigation_plan.question: Which hosts are encrypting, and is the count still rising?
investigation_plan.why: Decides containment scope. A rising count means contain now; a flat one means investigate first.

investigation_plan.question: What account is the encrypting process running as, and is it privileged?
investigation_plan.why: A domain admin changes the blast radius from one host to the estate.

investigation_plan.question: Did shadow copies or backups get deleted, and when relative to encryption?
investigation_plan.why: Determines whether recovery is possible without paying, which is the question leadership asks first.

investigation_plan.question: How did the process arrive — email, remote service, or existing foothold?
investigation_plan.why: Containing the host without closing the entry point means it happens again tonight.

investigation_plan.question: Are the file extensions or the ransom note attributable to a known family?
investigation_plan.why: Attribution changes the expected next step — some families exfiltrate before encrypting.

validation.action: Replay 200 rename events for one process within five minutes through the live windowed engine.
validation.expect: Exactly one alert, severity critical, technique T1486.

validation.action: Replay 199 of the same rename events — one short of the threshold.
validation.expect: No alert. A pack whose detections fire on benign activity is worse than no pack.

validation.action: Replay fixtures for all three detections within one 30-minute window on one host.
validation.expect: One correlated incident, not three alerts. This is the claim the correlation section makes.

validation.action: Run the response playbook in dry-run against a documentation-range host.
validation.expect: Every step reports a plan and nothing reports executed, confirming the approval gate holds.
